name: commons-threshold-3
description: ⭐ THE INFLOW CAP AT 3, THE LADDER AROUND THE ARM THAT MEASURED NOTHING (C10, Dean 09/09/2026). rules.economy.commonsThreshold 3: a central board already holding 3 cards REFUSES a further play until somebody Harvests it. The shipped rule is null, no cap, and this is the only thing in the commons that can refuse a play at all - so it is a change to C4 (“central boards have no threshold; nothing in the game refuses a play”) and not a tuning of it. At 3 the cap sits ABOVE the shipped median take of 2, so it should refuse even less than 2 did - it is the control that says whether the null result at 2 was the cap being too loose to matter or the semantic being wrong altogether. Expect nothing, and expecting nothing is the point: an arm that confirms a mechanism is dead is worth running once. Dean, 09/09/2026: “Can we measure how many cards are taken when the Harvest is done against the centre cards? I'm interested to see if we place a threshold on the centre cards if it will reduce the number of cards going from the centre to the barns - my target is about 30-40% of barn cards should come from the middle.” The centre share reads 63.1% on the shipped rules. ⛔ THE FIRST ANSWER MEASURED NOTHING, WHICH IS WHY THERE ARE THREE SEMANTICS AND NOT ONE. rules.economy.commonsThreshold at 2 - a cap on the INFLOW - moved the centre share by 0.1 points, 63.1% to 63.0%, for two reasons worth holding on to before running any of these: a central harvest already takes a MEDIAN OF TWO CARDS, so a cap of two caps almost nothing; and the centre is a CLOSED system, in by a play (C3) and out by a harvest (D3), so every card played into it reaches somebody's barn unless the game ends first. A cap on plays therefore changes WHEN cards leave the centre, not how many. ⭐ THE THREE SEMANTICS, NAMED SO NOBODY CONFUSES THEM: commonsThreshold caps the INFLOW (a pile at its cap refuses a play); commonsHarvestMin gates the OUTFLOW (a pile below n refuses a harvest - the BUILDING semantic, a pile is “full” at n); commonsHarvestTake caps the SIZE of the outflow and leaves the rest standing, which is the only one of the three that can reduce the centre's outflow WITHOUT reducing plays. ⚠️ READ EVERY ONE OF THEM AGAINST THE CONSERVATION LINE a18 PRINTS, which carries all three terms per game: plays into the centre = cards harvested out + cards stranded at game end. A knob that hits Dean's target by STRANDING cards has changed where the cards end up rather than how the centre feeds a barn during play, and that is a different answer to his question. ⚠️ AND SWEEP THEM ONE AT A TIME. Each of these files sets exactly ONE leaf and carries no passengers, which is the 05/09/2026 lesson: a joint move is unattributable. ⚠️ overlays/commons-threshold-2.overlay.json is the middle rung and the one already measured: it moved the centre share by 0.1 points. This file and its sibling at the other end exist so that the null result is a LADDER rather than a single point, which is the difference between “the cap was too loose” and “the cap cannot do this job”. ⚠️ AND THE INFLOW CAP HAS A SECOND-ORDER EFFECT THE OTHER TWO DO NOT: a full board is a RACE rather than a denial, because ANY player may empty it with a Harvest and take the pile. Watch the refusal rate - how often a seat wanted a board that was full - which is the blocked-want reading under a new name. READ IN THIS ORDER: (1) a18's centre share of harvested barn cards, pooled and by seat count, against the 30-40% target; (2) the conservation line, to see whether the share moved by harvesting less or by stranding more; (3) the distribution of cards taken per central harvest (1 / 2 / 3 / 4 / 5+), which says what any cap had to work with; (4) a17's bonus rate against Dean's 30-60% band, because a knob that makes the centre less rewarding can push plays out of the band at the other end; (5) the barn glut (a06) and deliveries per player, since the centre is a barn faucet and every one of these is a tap on it. ⛔ PASSENGERS PINNED 12/09/2026: Dean's plain-action balloon and Village Store ruling moved sixteen shipped leaves at once. This overlay predates that flip and every report taken against it does too, so each of those leaves is pinned here BY NAME at its PRE-FLIP value. Without it an arm read as a delta against a pre-flip base would silently gain a one-card flight, an always-present Aerodrome and a live coin economy. That is the 05/09/2026 passenger lesson: an overlay that should not move with the shipped default has to pin every knob the flip moved.
